The Book
“I stopped searching for myself when I realized I had never left where I came from.”

In these poems, a woman moves through illness, anger, research, memory, gardens, and ancestral wisdom in search of another way forward. Guided by the earth beneath her feet, she discovers that healing is not always found in certainty, but in relationship.

Part memoir, part myth, part invocation, Soil in My Veins asks what happens when we listen closely to the body and what we might remember when we listen to the earth.

Origin

I never intended to write a book.

I started writing because I needed somewhere to place the questions I carried after my health began to change. Poetry became my way of making sense of doctor’s appointments, uncertainty, and the quiet hope that healing might look different than I once imagined.

As the poems grew, I realized this story wasn’t only mine. Many people are searching for answers, connection, and permission to listen to their own bodies. I wanted to share my journey — not because it is universal, but because I hoped parts of it might resonate with someone else’s.

I’ve always loved mythology, especially the way ancient stories use nature to explore transformation. That love found its way into these poems, where roots, storms, seeds, and Gaia became symbols for the changes happening within me.

Soil in My Veins is my invitation to slow down, pay attention, and remember that sometimes healing begins with listening. If these poems help even one person feel a little less alone, then they’ve already taken root.

This is not a self-help guide. Not a wellness manual.

It is a remembrance — a meditation on what was always already here, beneath all the noise of becoming.

Excerpt

“Mother Earth breathes slowly when you are quiet enough.
Then she spoke.

Child, the seed breaks before it rises. Roots must claim the dark before a tree can meet the sun. Breathe. Metamorphosis is not gentle.”

About

Gaia is not
one person.

Gaia Roots is not built around a single creator. It is built around recognition.

Gaia is the name given to everyone who feels the Earth in themselves — not as concept, but as truth.

It belongs to no single voice, because it is carried by many.

G.A.I.A: Grounded Awareness In All.

Not a person. A posture. A way of being present to what is already here, already known, already rooted in the soil of who you are.

If you feel it, you are already part of it.
